text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success, and the SMART framework provides a useful guide. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. Instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal might be "increase user engagement by 20% within six months." Once your main goal is set, you should break it down into smaller milestones, such as completing the design phase by the end of the first month. Each milestone should have a clear deliverable, like a prototype or a report. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment so that everyone—from the team to the client—understands and agrees on the objectives. This shared understanding keeps the project focused and reduces confusion later on.
